newsitem.title: IRAN: Iran plans to rebuild quake areas with foreign aid.
newsitem.headline: Iran plans to rebuild quake areas with foreign aid.

text.p: Iran is drawing up a programme to rebuild, with the help of foreign donations, areas devastated by a deadly quake that flattened up to 20,000 houses, foreign aid workers said on Thursday.
Reconstruction, partly funded by international aid, of medical, educational and irrigation facilities destroyed by Saturday's quake would be the government's priority, a United Nations official said.

"Between 16,000 to 20,000 houses were destroyed...The total cost of the damage is 300 billion Iranian rials ($100 million)," the official, who has close working contacts with the Iranian government, told Reuters.
"The relief effort is completed. The Iranian government now wants to start reconstruction work in 20 days," he said.
Total damage from three major quakes that hit Iran this year was estimated at 600 billion rials ($200 million), he added.
Latest figures showed 52,000 villagers were made homeless by Saturday's quake in eastern Iran which measured 7.1 on the Richter scale, he said. There have been more than 250 aftershocks.
Iran said on Wednesday the death toll from the quake reached 1,568 and 15 people were missing. Some 2,300 were injured.

The quake flattened or heavily damaged 168 farming villages close to the towns of Qaen and Birjand in the Iranian province of Khorasan, destroying houses, schools and shops -- many of which were built with clay and straw bricks.

A report released on Thursday in Tehran by the U.N. World Food Programme (WFP) said food aid would be needed in the villages for the next three months "to get them back on their feet," a WFP official said.
Villages are currently getting supplies of bread, rice, biscuits, potatoes and clothing from storage and distribution centres run by the Iranian Red Crescent.
The badly hit villages around Qaen farmed saffron, berries and wheat and depended on regular water supplies from nearby mountains through irrigation ducts severly damaged by the quake.
The collapse of school buildings was one of the most tragic episodes of the disaster, with one village losing more than 60 pupils aged between six and 12 as they sat at their desks.

The Red Crescent has been distributing food, tents and other supplies to quake victims, supported by Iranian religous foundations and local volunteers. Aid supplies delivered by 16 countries reached 200 tonnes on Wednesday, state-run Tehran radio said.

The Geneva-based International Federation of Red Cross and Red Crescent Societies said it has raised seven million Swiss francs ($4.6 million) towards its 12 million Swiss franc appeal to help the quake victims.

Several countries have made pledges or said they have sent aid, including Iran's arch-foe the United States and European Union states involved in a diplomatic row with Tehran. ($1=3,000 rials at the official exchange rate)
